slide.title: Market equilibrium: demand, supply and price
slide.b1: Demand curve: quantity demanded falls as price rises, Qd = a − bP (ceteris paribus)
slide.b2: Supply curve: quantity supplied rises with price, Qs = c + dP
slide.b3: Equilibrium price P* where Qd = Qs; no excess demand, no excess supply
slide.b4: A shift in supply (harvest, input costs, technology) moves P* along the demand curve
slide.b5: Shortage at P < P* ⇒ price rises; surplus at P > P* ⇒ price falls

ask.q: Why does a bad harvest make bread expensive?
ask.a: Less grain means less bread at every price. At the old price more people want bread than there is, so bakers raise it until buyers and loaves match again.

prove.q: A frost kills half the coffee crop. The price…
prove.right: Right. Fewer bags at every price.
prove.wrong: Think about the queue at the old price.

lights.title: Every subject has its own light.

explain.headline: A price is where buyers and sellers stop arguing

parts.label: Demand
parts.body: The cheaper something is, the more people want it.
parts.spot: quantity demanded falls as price rises

parts.label: Supply
parts.body: The pricier it is, the more sellers show up.

parts.label: Where they meet
parts.body: At one price nobody is left waiting. That’s the market price.
parts.spot: no excess demand, no excess supply

steps.label: Shortage
steps.body: At the old price, buyers outnumber sellers.

steps.label: Price rises
steps.body: Sellers raise it until the queue is gone.
